# Rainbow — recovery guide

> **Newest procedure (2026-11-16):** one command, `bash scripts/claude-bootstrap.sh` — it also runs automatically
> at every Claude session start. See `backups/CLAUDE_ACCOUNT_TRANSFER.md` (top section). The branch names below are
> historical; the bootstrap always merges the newest `ccr-*`/`claude/*` branch.

How to restore the RAINBOW 11-screen 3D game on another computer or another Claude Code account.

## 1. Where the backup lives

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Repository | https://github.com/josiahscalia5-dev/rainbow- (**private**) |
| Working branch (continue here) | `claude/rainbow-3d-recovery-m4v347` — recovery branch started 2026-11-15 from commit `81e639e`; the 5-minute autosave pushes here |
| Original branch (frozen) | `ccr-6f431adf-7h0m8y` at `81e639e` — everything from the first Claude account; still the repo's default branch. Autosave refuses to push to it (`protected_branches` in `backups/autosave.config.json`) |
| Cloud environment | claude.ai environment **"rainbow-"**: its setup script (copy in `scripts/cloud-env-setup.sh`) restores LFS files, Android SDK 34, Blender 5.3.0 and the World Labs plugin in every fresh container |
| Live status | `backups/BACKUP_STATUS.json` (last run, last verified remote SHA) |
| Run history | `backups/BACKUP_LOG.md` |
| Where the project stands | `backups/CURRENT_STATE.md` |
| Claude conversations | `backups/CONVERSATION_INDEX.md` → `backups/claude-sessions/<session-id>/` |
| Specialist agents | `.claude/agents/*.md` + roster/status `backups/AGENTS_STATUS.md` |
| Tool/MCP reconnection | `backups/MCP_SETUP.md`, `.mcp.json.template` (no secrets) |
| Original upload package | `backups/source-package/` (kit ZIP via Git LFS + the two prompt files) |
| File checksums | `backups/MANIFEST.json` |

## 2. Clone

```bash
# Git LFS is required for the kit ZIP and any .glb/.blend/.apk assets
git lfs install
git clone https://github.com/josiahscalia5-dev/rainbow-.git rainbow
cd rainbow
git checkout claude/rainbow-3d-recovery-m4v347   # NOT the frozen original ccr-6f431adf-7h0m8y
git lfs pull            # downloads LFS objects (GLB models, kit ZIP, builds)
bash scripts/setup-android-sdk.sh && bash scripts/setup-blender.sh   # if the machine lacks them
```

Verify the locked references were not altered:

```bash
sha256sum -c <(grep -oE '`[0-9a-f]{64}`' REFERENCE_ORDER.md | tr -d '`' | paste - <(ls references/*.png; echo character_references/official_cartoon_girl_original.jpg) -d '  ')
# or simply compare against the SHA-256 table in REFERENCE_ORDER.md
```

## 3. Install & run the game

```bash
npm ci                   # Node 20+ (tested with Node 22)
npm run dev              # http://localhost:5173 — portrait game in the browser
npm run build            # production web build into dist/
npm run test:continuity  # route/altitude continuity test (07 plunge → 08 inlet)
npm run qa:capture       # Playwright: screenshots/01.png … 11.png + qa/ comparisons
```

Android (Capacitor): see `docs/BUILD_ANDROID.md`.

## 4. Re-enable the five-minute autosave on the new machine

```bash
bash scripts/install-autosave-scheduler.sh   # cron */5 (Linux) or loop-daemon fallback
python3 scripts/rainbow-autosave.py --reason manual   # one immediate backup + verification
```

* macOS: replace cron with a launchd agent that runs `scripts/autosave-cron.sh` every 300 s.
* Windows: Task Scheduler → "every 5 minutes" → `bash scripts/autosave-cron.sh` (Git Bash/WSL).
* Edit `backups/autosave.config.json` if the repo URL or branch changes — the script refuses to push
  anywhere that does not match it.
* Claude Code hooks (`.claude/settings.json`) re-arm the scheduler at every SessionStart and snapshot at
  PreCompact / Stop / SessionEnd automatically once the repo is opened in Claude Code.

## 5. Restore the specialists and tools

* The 10 specialists are plain files in `.claude/agents/`. Open the repo in Claude Code and they load as
  project subagents (check with `/agents`).
* Reconnect MCP servers with the commands in `backups/MCP_SETUP.md`. Add API keys only through each
  tool's sign-in flow or your local environment — never commit them.

## 6. Resume the Claude conversation

* A Git snapshot **cannot** revive a live in-memory Claude session or its hidden state.
* To continue: open the repo in Claude Code and say *"Read backups/CURRENT_STATE.md and the latest
  backups/claude-sessions/*/transcript.md, then continue Rainbow from the next task listed."*
* The sanitized transcripts omit hidden model reasoning and image payloads (the images are in
  `references/` and `screenshots/`), and redact e-mail addresses/secrets.

## 7. Limits you should know

* The current development machine is an **ephemeral cloud container**. Its cron job runs only while the
  container is alive; when the session is idle long enough the container is reclaimed and the schedule
  stops. Everything up to the last 5-minute push is safe on GitHub; the SessionStart hook re-arms the
  schedule the next time a session opens this repo.
* Nothing is ever force-pushed; if the remote diverges the script merges non-destructively or stops and
  logs the conflict, keeping the local commit.
* When starting a new cloud session, select the branch `claude/rainbow-3d-recovery-m4v347` (GitHub's
  default branch is still the frozen original). If the session gets a different branch name, the autosave
  refuses to push (branch mismatch is logged) until `backups/autosave.config.json` → `branch` is updated.
* 2026-11-15 recovery: the first account's session `515c677b…` stopped at 18:01 UTC (usage limit); the
  18:05 autosave (`81e639e`) captured its last edit. Nothing after that existed. Details:
  `backups/CURRENT_STATE.md`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Claude Code hook entry point:  autosave-hook.sh <SessionStart|PreCompact|Stop|SessionEnd>
# SessionStart -> scripts/claude-bootstrap.sh --hook: merges newer saved work, restores Git LFS, re-arms the
#   five-minute autosave, prints a short recovery summary for Claude and runs the full bootstrap in the background.
# Stop runs in the background so it never delays a turn (and re-arms the scheduler if it died);
# PreCompact/SessionEnd run one verified autosave inline (bounded).
EVENT="${1:-hook}"
REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
case "$EVENT" in
  SessionStart)
    if [ -f "$REPO/scripts/claude-bootstrap.sh" ]; then
      exec bash "$REPO/scripts/claude-bootstrap.sh" --hook     # reads the hook JSON (source) from stdin
    fi
    # fallback for an old checkout without the bootstrap
    cat > /dev/null 2>&1
    bash "$REPO/scripts/install-autosave-scheduler.sh" > "$HOME/.rainbow-autosave-install.log" 2>&1
    git -C "$REPO" config --unset-all "lfs.https://github.com/josiahscalia5-dev/rainbow-.git/info/lfs.access" 2>/dev/null

    cat > /dev/null 2>&1
    ;;
esac

1	"""Screen 05 proj05 — bake the TARGET water image (tools/proj05/make_target.py) onto the REAL game river, in the
2	river's own coordinates (u across -1..1, s = arc length), using the live game's per-pixel river coordinates from the
3	locked 05 camera (scripts/proj05-probe.mjs -> uv_river.f32). Everything is anchored to the river, not to the camera.
4	
5	usage: python3 -I tools/proj05/bake.py <probe_dir> <target_dir> <out_dir>
6	outputs (out_dir, default assets/textures/water05/):
7	  proj05_E.png   EXACT layer: the approved water at ~screen resolution; rows follow s with the locked view's own
8	                 density, columns span the locked view's visible u-range per row (lookup in proj05_lut.json); alpha = valid
9	  proj05_N.png   NEAR layer: same water, full river width, uniform 24 texels per unit of s for s in [sN0, sN1]; alpha = coverage
10	  proj05_T.png   TILE layer: seamless periodic copy of the full-width mid river (s period L) for the rest of Screen 05
11	  proj05_D.png   DETAIL layer: luminance high-pass of the sharpest near water (the approved streaks / glints), seamless
12	                 in u and s, 0.5 = no change
13	  proj05_F.png   FAR layer: the far river block (far05.ts) in its own (uv.x, log depth) coordinates; alpha = valid
14	  proj05_lut.json  s -> (V, centre u, half range u) for proj05_E + all layer extents
15	coins are filled along the flow (s direction) in river space."""
16	import json, os, sys
17	import numpy as np
18	from PIL import Image
19	from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter, gaussian_filter1d, binary_dilation, binary_erosion
20	
21	probe, tdir, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
22	os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
23	W, H = 864, 1536
24	R = np.fromfile(os.path.join(probe, "uv_river.f32"), np.float32).reshape(H, W, 4).astype(np.float64)
25	surf = np.abs(R[..., 2] - 1) < 0.01
26	wm = np.asarray(Image.open(os.path.join(tdir, "water_mask.png"))) > 127
27	# coins are filled in the target from the user's artwork (make_target.py); the along-s hole filling below stays for gaps
28	coin = np.zeros((H, W), bool)
29	tgt = np.asarray(Image.open(os.path.join(tdir, "target_05.png")).convert("RGB"), np.float64) / 255
30	# colour feedback from the live capture (tools/proj05/residual.py): what the bloom pass adds is taken out of the bake
31	if os.path.exists(os.path.join(tdir, "correction.npz")):
32	    tgt = np.clip(tgt - np.load(os.path.join(tdir, "correction.npz"))["c"].astype(np.float64), 0, 1)
33	U, S = R[..., 0], R[..., 1]
34	S_CUT = 182.0                                   # the real ribbon ends behind the far block's seam
35	use = surf & wm & (S < S_CUT)
36	ys, xs = np.nonzero(use)
37	su, ss, sc, scoin = U[use], S[use], tgt[use], coin[use]
38	# locked-view density along s (screen rows per unit s), per pixel
39	dsy = np.abs(np.gradient(S, axis=0))
40	
41	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- E (exact) layer
42	sE0, sE1 = float(ss.min()) - 0.02, float(ss.max()) + 0.02
43	NL = 2048
44	sg = np.linspace(sE0, sE1, NL)
45	bin_i = np.clip(((ss - sE0) / (sE1 - sE0) * (NL - 1)).round().astype(int), 0, NL - 1)
46	umin = np.full(NL, np.nan); umax = np.full(NL, np.nan); dens = np.full(NL, np.nan)
47	order = np.argsort(bin_i); bi = bin_i[order]
48	starts = np.searchsorted(bi, np.arange(NL)); ends = np.searchsorted(bi, np.arange(NL), side="right")
49	dsel = dsy[use][order]; usel = su[order]
50	for k in range(NL):
51	    a, b = starts[k], ends[k]
52	    if b - a >= 3:
53	        uu = usel[a:b]
54	        umin[k], umax[k] = uu.min(), uu.max()
55	        dens[k] = 1.0 / max(np.median(dsel[a:b]), 1e-4)
56	def fill_nan(v):
57	    i = np.arange(len(v)); ok = np.isfinite(v)
58	    return np.interp(i, i[ok], v[ok])
59	umin, umax, dens = fill_nan(umin), fill_nan(umax), fill_nan(dens)
60	# u-range: running min / max over +-6 bins, then smooth (no wiggles), 1.5 % margin
61	from scipy.ndimage import minimum_filter1d, maximum_filter1d
62	umin = gaussian_filter1d(minimum_filter1d(umin, 25), 6) - 0.015
63	umax = gaussian_filter1d(maximum_filter1d(umax, 25), 6) + 0.015
64	umin, umax = np.clip(umin, -1, 1), np.clip(umax, -1, 1)
65	cE, wE = (umin + umax) / 2, np.maximum((umax - umin) / 2, 0.02)
66	dens = np.exp(gaussian_filter1d(np.log(np.clip(dens, 1, 400)), 8))
67	tex_d = np.maximum(dens * 1.3, 8.0)                  # texel rows per unit s (>= 8: the far rows stay sharp at the locked eye)
68	cum = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum((tex_d[1:] + tex_d[:-1]) / 2 * np.diff(sg))])
69	NE = int(min(2048, np.ceil(cum[-1])))
70	V = cum / cum[-1]
71	WE = 1024
72	def e_coords(u, s):
73	    v = np.interp(s, sg, V); c = np.interp(s, sg, cE); w = np.interp(s, sg, wE)
74	    return (0.5 + (u - c) / (2 * w)) * WE - 0.5, v * NE - 0.5
75	
76	def splat(xf, yf, col, Wt, Ht):
77	    acc = np.zeros((Ht, Wt, col.shape[1])); wt = np.zeros((Ht, Wt))
78	    x0 = np.floor(xf).astype(int); y0 = np.floor(yf).astype(int); fx = xf - x0; fy = yf - y0
79	    for dx, dy, ww in ((0, 0, (1 - fx) * (1 - fy)), (1, 0, fx * (1 - fy)), (0, 1, (1 - fx) * fy), (1, 1, fx * fy)):
80	        xi, yi = x0 + dx, y0 + dy
81	        ok = (xi >= 0) & (xi < Wt) & (yi >= 0) & (yi < Ht)
82	        np.add.at(acc, (yi[ok], xi[ok]), col[ok] * ww[ok, None]); np.add.at(wt, (yi[ok], xi[ok]), ww[ok])
83	    return acc, wt
84	
85	def finish(acc, wt, holew, fill_sigma=1.2, along_axis=0, max_gap=400, fill_all=False):
86	    """normalise; fill tiny gaps by normalised blur; coin holes by linear interpolation along s (axis 0)."""
87	    img = acc / np.maximum(wt, 1e-9)[..., None]
88	    valid = wt > 0.2
89	    hole = holew > np.maximum(wt, 1e-9) * 0.5         # coin pixels dominate this texel
90	    valid &= ~hole
91	    blur_w = gaussian_filter(valid.astype(float), fill_sigma)
92	    blur_c = np.stack([gaussian_filter(np.where(valid, img[..., i], 0), fill_sigma) for i in range(img.shape[2])], -1)
93	    gap = (~valid) & (blur_w > 0.12) & ~binary_dilation(hole, iterations=1)
94	    img[gap] = (blur_c / np.maximum(blur_w, 1e-6)[..., None])[gap]
95	    valid = valid | gap
96	    # coin holes: interpolate along s (columns), between valid texels at both ends
97	    hole_t = (binary_dilation(hole, iterations=2) & ~valid | hole) if not fill_all else (~valid | hole)
98	    Ht, Wt = valid.shape
99	    filled = np.zeros_like(valid)
100	    for x in range(Wt):
101	        col_h = hole_t[:, x]
102	        if not col_h.any(): continue
103	        vcol = valid[:, x] & ~col_h
104	        idx = np.nonzero(vcol)[0]
105	        if len(idx) < 2: continue
106	        hy = np.nonzero(col_h)[0]
107	        lo = np.searchsorted(idx, hy) - 1; hi = lo + 1
108	        ok = (lo >= 0) & (hi < len(idx))
109	        hy, lo, hi = hy[ok], lo[ok], hi[ok]
110	        y0_, y1_ = idx[lo], idx[hi]
111	        ok = (y1_ - y0_) <= max_gap
112	        hy, y0_, y1_ = hy[ok], y0_[ok], y1_[ok]
113	        t = ((hy - y0_) / np.maximum(y1_ - y0_, 1))[:, None]
114	        img[hy, x] = img[y0_, x] * (1 - t) + img[y1_, x] * t
115	        filled[hy, x] = True
116	    # soften the interpolated stripes across u a little
117	    if filled.any():
118	        sm = np.stack([gaussian_filter(img[..., i], (0.6, 1.5)) for i in range(img.shape[2])], -1)
119	        img[filled] = sm[filled]
120	    valid = valid | filled
121	    finish.filled = filled
122	    return img, valid
123	
124	xE, yE = e_coords(su, ss)
125	accE, _ = splat(xE, yE, np.where(scoin[:, None], 0, sc), WE, NE)
126	holeE, _ = splat(xE, yE, scoin[:, None].astype(float), WE, NE)
127	wtE, _ = splat(xE, yE, (~scoin)[:, None].astype(float), WE, NE)
128	E, validE = finish(accE, wtE[..., 0], holeE[..., 0], max_gap=int(NE * 0.35))
129	alphaE = gaussian_filter(binary_erosion(validE, iterations=1).astype(float), 0.8)
130	
131	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- N (near, full width) layer
132	sN0, sN1, dN, WN = 126.0, 166.0, 24, 512
133	NN = int((sN1 - sN0) * dN)
134	xN = (su + 1) / 2 * WN - 0.5; yN = (ss - sN0) * dN - 0.5
135	accN, _ = splat(xN, yN, np.where(scoin[:, None], 0, sc), WN, NN)
136	holeN, _ = splat(xN, yN, scoin[:, None].astype(float), WN, NN)
137	wtN, _ = splat(xN, yN, (~scoin)[:, None].astype(float), WN, NN)
138	N_, validN = finish(accN, wtN[..., 0], holeN[..., 0], fill_sigma=1.5, max_gap=int(12 * dN), fill_all=True)
139	realN = validN & ~finish.filled                    # texels that saw real approved water (not coin / gap fills)
140	# fill the remaining (unseen) gaps inside N by a wide normalised blur, but keep them flagged as weak
141	covN = gaussian_filter(validN.astype(float), 3.0)
142	alphaN = np.clip((covN - 0.35) / 0.5, 0, 1)
143	# where the locked eye saw the river only at low density (far rows) the near layer would be a blurred copy: the
144	# crisp tile takes over there (rows weighted by the locked view's own density, < 6 rows / unit -> 0, > 14 -> 1)
145	srow = sN0 + (np.arange(NN) + 0.5) / dN
146	alphaN *= np.clip((np.interp(srow, sg, dens) - 6.0) / 8.0, 0, 1)[:, None]
147	
148	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- T (periodic tile) layer
149	# the crisp near river (s 134-151: hot-pink ribbons and cyan core at high locked density), as LAYOUT (the detail layer
150	# adds the fine streaks): rows interpolated; the bank the locked eye does not see is the mirror of the other bank, then
151	# the column mean, with smooth weights (no hard fill edges); periodic with a 3-unit crossfade at the wrap
152	a_s, L, b = 134.0, 14.0, 3.0
153	NT = int(L * dN)
154	def rows_at(img, s_):
155	    y = np.clip((s_ - sN0) * dN - 0.5, 0, NN - 1.001); y0 = np.floor(y).astype(int); f = (y - y0)[:, None]
156	    return img[y0] * (1 - f[..., None] if img.ndim == 3 else 1 - f) + img[y0 + 1] * (f[..., None] if img.ndim == 3 else f)

"""Screen 05 proj05 — bake the TARGET water image (tools/proj05/make_target.py) onto the REAL game river, in the
river's own coordinates (u across -1..1, s = arc length), using the live game's per-pixel river coordinates from the
locked 05 camera (scripts/proj05-probe.mjs -> uv_river.f32). Everything is anchored to the river, not to the camera.

usage: python3 -I tools/proj05/bake.py <probe_dir> <target_dir> <out_dir>
outputs (out_dir, default assets/textures/water05/):
  proj05_E.png   EXACT layer: the approved water at ~screen resolution; rows follow s with the locked view's own
                 density, columns span the locked view's visible u-range per row (lookup in proj05_lut.json); alpha = valid
  proj05_N.png   NEAR layer: same water, full river width, uniform 24 texels per unit of s for s in [sN0, sN1]; alpha = coverage
  proj05_T.png   TILE layer: seamless periodic copy of the full-width mid river (s period L) for the rest of Screen 05
  proj05_D.png   DETAIL layer: luminance high-pass of the sharpest near water (the approved streaks / glints), seamless
                 in u and s, 0.5 = no change
  proj05_F.png   FAR layer: the far river block (far05.ts) in its own (uv.x, log depth) coordinates; alpha = valid
  proj05_lut.json  s -> (V, centre u, half range u) for proj05_E + all layer extents
coins are filled along the flow (s direction) in river space."""
import json, os, sys
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter, gaussian_filter1d, binary_dilation, binary_erosion

probe, tdir, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
W, H = 864, 1536
R = np.fromfile(os.path.join(probe, "uv_river.f32"), np.float32).reshape(H, W, 4).astype(np.float64)
surf = np.abs(R[..., 2] - 1) < 0.01
wm = np.asarray(Image.open(os.path.join(tdir, "water_mask.png"))) > 127
# coins are filled in the target from the user's artwork (make_target.py); the along-s hole filling below stays for gaps
coin = np.zeros((H, W), bool)
tgt = np.asarray(Image.open(os.path.join(tdir, "target_05.png")).convert("RGB"), np.float64) / 255
# colour feedback from the live capture (tools/proj05/residual.py): what the bloom pass adds is taken out of the bake
if os.path.exists(os.path.join(tdir, "correction.npz")):
    tgt = np.clip(tgt - np.load(os.path.join(tdir, "correction.npz"))["c"].astype(np.float64), 0, 1)
U, S = R[..., 0], R[..., 1]
S_CUT = 182.0                                   # the real ribbon ends behind the far block's seam
use = surf & wm & (S < S_CUT)
ys, xs = np.nonzero(use)
su, ss, sc, scoin = U[use], S[use], tgt[use], coin[use]
# locked-view density along s (screen rows per unit s), per pixel
dsy = np.abs(np.gradient(S, axis=0))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- E (exact) layer
sE0, sE1 = float(ss.min()) - 0.02, float(ss.max()) + 0.02
NL = 2048
sg = np.linspace(sE0, sE1, NL)
bin_i = np.clip(((ss - sE0) / (sE1 - sE0) * (NL - 1)).round().astype(int), 0, NL - 1)
umin = np.full(NL, np.nan); umax = np.full(NL, np.nan); dens = np.full(NL, np.nan)
order = np.argsort(bin_i); bi = bin_i[order]
starts = np.searchsorted(bi, np.arange(NL)); ends = np.searchsorted(bi, np.arange(NL), side="right")
dsel = dsy[use][order]; usel = su[order]
for k in range(NL):
    a, b = starts[k], ends[k]
    if b - a >= 3:
        uu = usel[a:b]
        umin[k], umax[k] = uu.min(), uu.max()
        dens[k] = 1.0 / max(np.median(dsel[a:b]), 1e-4)
def fill_nan(v):
    i = np.arange(len(v)); ok = np.isfinite(v)
    return np.interp(i, i[ok], v[ok])
umin, umax, dens = fill_nan(umin), fill_nan(umax), fill_nan(dens)
# u-range: running min / max over +-6 bins, then smooth (no wiggles), 1.5 % margin
from scipy.ndimage import minimum_filter1d, maximum_filter1d
umin = gaussian_filter1d(minimum_filter1d(umin, 25), 6) - 0.015
umax = gaussian_filter1d(maximum_filter1d(umax, 25), 6) + 0.015
umin, umax = np.clip(umin, -1, 1), np.clip(umax, -1, 1)
cE, wE = (umin + umax) / 2, np.maximum((umax - umin) / 2, 0.02)
dens = np.exp(gaussian_filter1d(np.log(np.clip(dens, 1, 400)), 8))
tex_d = np.maximum(dens * 1.3, 8.0)                  # texel rows per unit s (>= 8: the far rows stay sharp at the locked eye)
cum = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum((tex_d[1:] + tex_d[:-1]) / 2 * np.diff(sg))])
NE = int(min(2048, np.ceil(cum[-1])))
V = cum / cum[-1]
WE = 1024
def e_coords(u, s):
    v = np.interp(s, sg, V); c = np.interp(s, sg, cE); w = np.interp(s, sg, wE)
    return (0.5 + (u - c) / (2 * w)) * WE - 0.5, v * NE - 0.5

def splat(xf, yf, col, Wt, Ht):
    acc = np.zeros((Ht, Wt, col.shape[1])); wt = np.zeros((Ht, Wt))
    x0 = np.floor(xf).astype(int); y0 = np.floor(yf).astype(int); fx = xf - x0; fy = yf - y0
    for dx, dy, ww in ((0, 0, (1 - fx) * (1 - fy)), (1, 0, fx * (1 - fy)), (0, 1, (1 - fx) * fy), (1, 1, fx * fy)):
        xi, yi = x0 + dx, y0 + dy
        ok = (xi >= 0) & (xi < Wt) & (yi >= 0) & (yi < Ht)
        np.add.at(acc, (yi[ok], xi[ok]), col[ok] * ww[ok, None]); np.add.at(wt, (yi[ok], xi[ok]), ww[ok])
    return acc, wt

def finish(acc, wt, holew, fill_sigma=1.2, along_axis=0, max_gap=400, fill_all=False):
    """normalise; fill tiny gaps by normalised blur; coin holes by linear interpolation along s (axis 0)."""
    img = acc / np.maximum(wt, 1e-9)[..., None]
    valid = wt > 0.2
    hole = holew > np.maximum(wt, 1e-9) * 0.5         # coin pixels dominate this texel
    valid &= ~hole
    blur_w = gaussian_filter(valid.astype(float), fill_sigma)
    blur_c = np.stack([gaussian_filter(np.where(valid, img[..., i], 0), fill_sigma) for i in range(img.shape[2])], -1)
    gap = (~valid) & (blur_w > 0.12) & ~binary_dilation(hole, iterations=1)
    img[gap] = (blur_c / np.maximum(blur_w, 1e-6)[..., None])[gap]
    valid = valid | gap
    # coin holes: interpolate along s (columns), between valid texels at both ends
    hole_t = (binary_dilation(hole, iterations=2) & ~valid | hole) if not fill_all else (~valid | hole)
    Ht, Wt = valid.shape
    filled = np.zeros_like(valid)
    for x in range(Wt):
        col_h = hole_t[:, x]
        if not col_h.any(): continue
        vcol = valid[:, x] & ~col_h
        idx = np.nonzero(vcol)[0]
        if len(idx) < 2: continue
        hy = np.nonzero(col_h)[0]
        lo = np.searchsorted(idx, hy) - 1; hi = lo + 1
        ok = (lo >= 0) & (hi < len(idx))
        hy, lo, hi = hy[ok], lo[ok], hi[ok]
        y0_, y1_ = idx[lo], idx[hi]
        ok = (y1_ - y0_) <= max_gap
        hy, y0_, y1_ = hy[ok], y0_[ok], y1_[ok]
        t = ((hy - y0_) / np.maximum(y1_ - y0_, 1))[:, None]
        img[hy, x] = img[y0_, x] * (1 - t) + img[y1_, x] * t
        filled[hy, x] = True
    # soften the interpolated stripes across u a little
    if filled.any():
        sm = np.stack([gaussian_filter(img[..., i], (0.6, 1.5)) for i in range(img.shape[2])], -1)
        img[filled] = sm[filled]
    valid = valid | filled
    finish.filled = filled
    return img, valid

xE, yE = e_coords(su, ss)
accE, _ = splat(xE, yE, np.where(scoin[:, None], 0, sc), WE, NE)
holeE, _ = splat(xE, yE, scoin[:, None].astype(float), WE, NE)
wtE, _ = splat(xE, yE, (~scoin)[:, None].astype(float), WE, NE)
E, validE = finish(accE, wtE[..., 0], holeE[..., 0], max_gap=int(NE * 0.35))
alphaE = gaussian_filter(binary_erosion(validE, iterations=1).astype(float), 0.8)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- N (near, full width) layer
sN0, sN1, dN, WN = 126.0, 166.0, 24, 512
NN = int((sN1 - sN0) * dN)
xN = (su + 1) / 2 * WN - 0.5; yN = (ss - sN0) * dN - 0.5
accN, _ = splat(xN, yN, np.where(scoin[:, None], 0, sc), WN, NN)
holeN, _ = splat(xN, yN, scoin[:, None].astype(float), WN, NN)
wtN, _ = splat(xN, yN, (~scoin)[:, None].astype(float), WN, NN)
N_, validN = finish(accN, wtN[..., 0], holeN[..., 0], fill_sigma=1.5, max_gap=int(12 * dN), fill_all=True)
realN = validN & ~finish.filled                    # texels that saw real approved water (not coin / gap fills)
# fill the remaining (unseen) gaps inside N by a wide normalised blur, but keep them flagged as weak
covN = gaussian_filter(validN.astype(float), 3.0)
alphaN = np.clip((covN - 0.35) / 0.5, 0, 1)
# where the locked eye saw the river only at low density (far rows) the near layer would be a blurred copy: the
# crisp tile takes over there (rows weighted by the locked view's own density, < 6 rows / unit -> 0, > 14 -> 1)
srow = sN0 + (np.arange(NN) + 0.5) / dN
alphaN *= np.clip((np.interp(srow, sg, dens) - 6.0) / 8.0, 0, 1)[:, None]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- T (periodic tile) layer
# the crisp near river (s 134-151: hot-pink ribbons and cyan core at high locked density), as LAYOUT (the detail layer
# adds the fine streaks): rows interpolated; the bank the locked eye does not see is the mirror of the other bank, then
# the column mean, with smooth weights (no hard fill edges); periodic with a 3-unit crossfade at the wrap
a_s, L, b = 134.0, 14.0, 3.0
NT = int(L * dN)
def rows_at(img, s_):
    y = np.clip((s_ - sN0) * dN - 0.5, 0, NN - 1.001); y0 = np.floor(y).astype(int); f = (y - y0)[:, None]
    return img[y0] * (1 - f[..., None] if img.ndim == 3 else 1 - f) + img[y0 + 1] * (f[..., None] if img.ndim == 3 else f)
sl = a_s + (np.arange(NT) + 0.5) / dN
# the tile trusts only texels that saw real water; everything else is first replaced by its column mean
colmeanN = (N_ * realN[..., None]).sum(0) / np.maximum(realN.sum(0), 1)[:, None]
N_t = np.where(realN[..., None], N_, colmeanN[None])
vN = np.clip((gaussian_filter(realN.astype(float), 2.0) - 0.5) * 2, 0, 1)
def layer(s_):
    c = rows_at(N_t, s_); w = rows_at(vN, s_)
    cm, wm_ = c[:, ::-1], w[:, ::-1]                      # mirrored bank
    colmean = (c * w[..., None]).sum(0) / np.maximum(w.sum(0), 1e-6)[:, None]
    w1 = np.clip(w, 0, 1); w2 = np.clip(wm_, 0, 1) * (1 - w1)
    w3 = np.clip(1 - w1 - w2, 0, 1)
    return (c * w1[..., None] + cm * w2[..., None] + colmean[None] * w3[..., None]) / np.maximum(w1 + w2 + w3, 1e-6)[..., None]
T_ = layer(sl)
blendr = sl - a_s < b
r = ((sl[blendr] - a_s) / b)[:, None, None]
T_[blendr] = layer(sl[blendr] + L) * (1 - r) + T_[blendr] * r
T_ = np.stack([gaussian_filter(T_[..., i], (3.0, 1.5), mode=("wrap", "nearest")) for i in range(3)], -1)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- D (detail) layer
# streaky, glinting water under Benny (the user's isolated artwork, no bubbles or coins): s in [131.5, 134.3], u in [-0.18, 0.18]
du0, du1, ds0, ds1 = -0.18, 0.18, 131.5, 134.3
ND = 512
m = (su > du0 - 0.03) & (su < du1 + 0.03) & (ss > ds0 - 0.1) & (ss < ds1 + 0.1)
lum = (sc[m] * np.array([0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722])).sum(1)
pad = 0.12                                    # crossfade fraction for seamless wrap
Wd = int(ND * (1 + pad)); Hd = int(ND * (1 + pad))
xd = (su[m] - du0) / (du1 - du0) * Wd - 0.5
yd = (ss[m] - ds0) / (ds1 - ds0) * Hd - 0.5
accD, wtD = splat(xd, yd, lum[:, None], Wd, Hd)
Dimg = accD[..., 0] / np.maximum(wtD, 1e-9)
okD = wtD > 0.05
bw = gaussian_filter(okD.astype(float), 1.5); bc = gaussian_filter(np.where(okD, Dimg, 0), 1.5)
Dimg = np.where(okD, Dimg, bc / np.maximum(bw, 1e-6))
hp = Dimg - gaussian_filter(Dimg, 14)          # high-pass: streaks, glints
p = int(ND * pad)
def wrap_axis(a, axis):
    a = np.moveaxis(a, axis, 0)
    n = a.shape[0] - p
    outa = a[:n].copy()
    r = (np.arange(p) / p)[:, None]
    outa[:p] = a[n:n + p] * (1 - r) + a[:p] * r
    return np.moveaxis(outa, 0, axis)
hpw = wrap_axis(wrap_axis(hp, 0), 1)
D = np.clip(0.5 + hpw * 1.0, 0, 1)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- F (far river block) layer
# the forced-perspective far river (far05.ts): its own coordinates (uv.x across the floor chord, virtual depth Z)
farm = (np.abs(R[..., 2] - 3) < 0.01) & wm
fx_, fz_ = R[..., 0][farm], R[..., 1][farm]
fcol, fcoin = tgt[farm], coin[farm]
ZMAX = float(max(fz_.max(), 1.0)) if farm.any() else 400.0
WF_, HF_ = 512, 512
xF = fx_ * WF_ - 0.5; yF = np.log1p(np.maximum(fz_, 0)) / np.log1p(ZMAX) * HF_ - 0.5
accF, _ = splat(xF, yF, np.where(fcoin[:, None], 0, fcol), WF_, HF_)
holeF, _ = splat(xF, yF, fcoin[:, None].astype(float), WF_, HF_)
wtF, _ = splat(xF, yF, (~fcoin)[:, None].astype(float), WF_, HF_)
F_, validF = finish(accF, wtF[..., 0], holeF[..., 0], fill_sigma=1.5, max_gap=80, fill_all=True)
alphaF = np.clip((gaussian_filter(validF.astype(float), 1.5) - 0.3) / 0.5, 0, 1)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- A (bank strip) layer
# the visual-only strip on the lower wall (src/vfx/proj05Apron.ts): x = 0.5 + 0.5 * t * side, y = s over [A_S0, A_S1]
A_S0, A_S1, WA, dA = 126.0, 190.0, 256, 12
HA = int((A_S1 - A_S0) * dA)
apm = (np.abs(R[..., 2] - 5) < 0.01) & wm
if apm.any():
    xa = (0.5 + 0.5 * R[..., 0][apm]) * WA - 0.5; ya = (R[..., 1][apm] - A_S0) * dA - 0.5
    accA, _ = splat(xa, ya, tgt[apm], WA, HA)
    wtA, _ = splat(xa, ya, np.ones((int(apm.sum()), 1)), WA, HA)
    A_, validA = finish(accA, wtA[..., 0], np.zeros((HA, WA)), fill_sigma=1.5, max_gap=int(3 * dA), fill_all=False)
    alphaA = np.clip((gaussian_filter(validA.astype(float), 1.2) - 0.3) / 0.5, 0, 1)
else:
    A_, alphaA = np.zeros((HA, WA, 3)), np.zeros((HA, WA))

def save(img, a, name):
    rgba = np.concatenate([np.clip(img, 0, 1), np.clip(a, 0, 1)[..., None]], -1) if a is not None else np.clip(img, 0, 1)
    Image.fromarray((rgba * 255 + 0.5).astype(np.uint8)).save(os.path.join(out, name), optimize=True)
save(F_, alphaF, "proj05_F.png"); save(A_, alphaA, "proj05_A.png"); save(E, alphaE, "proj05_E.png"); save(N_, alphaN, "proj05_N.png"); save(T_, None, "proj05_T.png")
Image.fromarray((D * 255 + 0.5).astype(np.uint8)).save(os.path.join(out, "proj05_D.png"), optimize=True)

LUTN = 1024
sl_ = np.linspace(sE0, sE1, LUTN)
lut = dict(
    note="Screen 05 proj05 bake (tools/proj05/bake.py). E: s -> V (row), c (centre u), w (half range u); v grows with s.",
    E=dict(s0=sE0, s1=sE1, n=LUTN, width=WE, height=NE,
           V=[round(float(x), 7) for x in np.interp(sl_, sg, V)], c=[round(float(x), 5) for x in np.interp(sl_, sg, cE)],
           w=[round(float(x), 5) for x in np.interp(sl_, sg, wE)]),
    N=dict(s0=sN0, s1=sN1, width=WN, height=NN), T=dict(a=a_s, L=L, width=WN, height=NT),
    D=dict(u0=du0, u1=du1, s0=ds0, s1=ds1, size=int(Wd - p), lum_gain=1.0),
    F=dict(zmax=ZMAX, width=WF_, height=HF_, note="far block: x = uv.x, y = log(1 + Z) / log(1 + zmax)"),
    probe_camera_uTime=12)
json.dump(lut, open(os.path.join(out, "proj05_lut.json"), "w"))
rep = dict(A_px=int(apm.sum()), E=[WE, NE], N=[WN, NN], T=[WN, NT], D=[int(Wd - p), int(Hd - p)], E_valid=float(validE.mean()), N_valid=float(validN.mean()),
           samples=int(use.sum()), coin_pixels=int(scoin.sum()), sE=[sE0, sE1])
print(json.dumps(rep))

1	"""Screen 05 approved-water FLOW MAP (`?proj05=1&projflow05=2`, src/vfx/waterRibbon.ts): the direction in which the
2	approved picture's own streaks run, read from the baked water layers in river coordinates (u across -1..1, s = arc
3	length), so the flow animation slides the fine streaks ALONG the painted S-curves instead of sliding the whole picture
4	straight down the river (which doubles the pink ribbons, the foam banks and the bubbles twice per cycle).
5	  proj05_WN.png  from the near layer N (s 126..166)      R = 0.5 + m * SCALE, m = du/ds along the streak (u per s unit)
6	  proj05_WT.png  from the periodic tile T (14 u, wraps)  G = flow mask: 1 streaky water … 0 foam banks, bubbles, edges
7	                                                          B = coverage of the layer (N: what the locked view shows; T: 1)
8	Method: structure tensor of luminance + red (pink vs cyan) on an isotropic resampling (PX px per world unit), the
9	streak direction = eigenvector of the smaller eigenvalue; slopes are averaged with coherence weights (normalised
10	convolution, sigma SMOOTH u) so flat or lumpy areas inherit the direction of the streaks around them.
11	usage: python3 -I tools/proj05/flow_bake.py <assets/textures/water05> [half_width_u=4.8] [--debug=DIR]"""
12	import json, os, sys
13	import numpy as np, cv2
14	from PIL import Image
15	from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter, binary_opening, binary_dilation
16	
17	pos = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if not a.startswith("--")]

"""Screen 05 approved-water FLOW MAP (`?proj05=1&projflow05=2`, src/vfx/waterRibbon.ts): the direction in which the
approved picture's own streaks run, read from the baked water layers in river coordinates (u across -1..1, s = arc
length), so the flow animation slides the fine streaks ALONG the painted S-curves instead of sliding the whole picture
straight down the river (which doubles the pink ribbons, the foam banks and the bubbles twice per cycle).
  proj05_WN.png  from the near layer N (s 126..166)      R = 0.5 + m * SCALE, m = du/ds along the streak (u per s unit)
  proj05_WT.png  from the periodic tile T (14 u, wraps)  G = flow mask: 1 streaky water … 0 foam banks, bubbles, edges
                                                          B = coverage of the layer (N: what the locked view shows; T: 1)
Method: structure tensor of luminance + red (pink vs cyan) on an isotropic resampling (PX px per world unit), the
streak direction = eigenvector of the smaller eigenvalue; slopes are averaged with coherence weights (normalised
convolution, sigma SMOOTH u) so flat or lumpy areas inherit the direction of the streaks around them.
usage: python3 -I tools/proj05/flow_bake.py <assets/textures/water05> [half_width_u=4.8] [--debug=DIR]"""
import json, os, sys
import numpy as np, cv2
from PIL import Image
from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter, binary_opening, binary_dilation

pos = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if not a.startswith("--")]
dbg = next((a.split("=", 1)[1] for a in sys.argv[1:] if a.startswith("--debug=")), None)
A = pos[0]
HW = float(pos[1]) if len(pos) > 1 else 4.8          # river half width (world units) ≈ course.widthAt(05) / 2
PX = 24.0                                             # isotropic working resolution, px per world unit
SCALE = 2.0                                           # R = 0.5 + m * SCALE  (|m| <= 0.25 u per s unit)
SMOOTH = 0.9                                          # world units
OUT_W = 128
lut = json.load(open(os.path.join(A, "proj05_lut.json")))


def flow_of(rgb, cov, length_u, wrap):
    """rgb float (h, w, 3) covering u -1..1 across and `length_u` world units along; returns m, mask, coherence"""
    h0, w0 = rgb.shape[:2]
    W, H = int(round(2 * HW * PX)), int(round(length_u * PX))
    img = cv2.resize(rgb, (W, H), interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)
    cv = cv2.resize(cov, (W, H), interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)
    mode = "wrap" if wrap else "nearest"
    g = lambda a, s: gaussian_filter(a, s, mode=("wrap" if wrap else "nearest", "nearest"))
    lum = (img * [0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722]).sum(-1)
    Jxx = Jxy = Jyy = 0.0
    for ch, wgt in ((lum, 1.0), (img[..., 0], 1.0)):
        c = g(ch, 1.2)
        gy, gx = np.gradient(c)
        if wrap:
            gy = (np.roll(c, -1, 0) - np.roll(c, 1, 0)) / 2
        Jxx = Jxx + wgt * gx * gx; Jxy = Jxy + wgt * gx * gy; Jyy = Jyy + wgt * gy * gy
    s_t = 0.45 * PX
    Jxx, Jxy, Jyy = g(Jxx, s_t), g(Jxy, s_t), g(Jyy, s_t)
    # eigenvector of the SMALLER eigenvalue = along the streaks
    tr, det = Jxx + Jyy, Jxx * Jyy - Jxy * Jxy
    disc = np.sqrt(np.maximum(tr * tr / 4 - det, 0))
    l1, l2 = tr / 2 + disc, tr / 2 - disc
    vx, vy = Jxy, l2 - Jxx                          # (J - l2 I) v = 0  ->  v = (Jxy, l2 - Jxx)
    alt = np.abs(vx) + np.abs(vy) < 1e-9
    vx = np.where(alt, 0.0, vx); vy = np.where(alt, 1.0, vy)
    sgn = np.where(vy < 0, -1.0, 1.0)
    vx, vy = vx * sgn, vy * sgn                     # pointing toward +s
    slope = np.clip(vx / np.maximum(vy, 1e-3), -1.2, 1.2)      # world dx per world ds
    coh = np.where(tr > 1e-6, (l1 - l2) / np.maximum(l1 + l2, 1e-6), 0.0)
    # foam banks + bubbles: bright, unsaturated, larger than a glint (opening drops thin highlights)
    mn, mx = img.min(-1), img.max(-1)
    whitish = (mn > 150) & (mx - mn < 80)
    blob = binary_opening(whitish, iterations=int(round(0.14 * PX)))
    blob = binary_dilation(blob, iterations=int(round(0.2 * PX)))
    still = g(blob.astype(np.float32), 0.35 * PX)
    uu = np.linspace(-1, 1, W)[None, :] * np.ones((H, 1))
    edge = 1.0 - np.clip((np.abs(uu) - 0.9) / 0.1, 0, 1)        # no flow offset on the very edge of the river
    mask = np.clip(1.0 - 1.6 * still, 0, 1) * edge
    # coherence-weighted average of the slope; foam / flat areas inherit the streak direction around them
    wgt = np.clip(coh, 0, 1) ** 2 * (1.0 - np.clip(still * 2, 0, 1)) * np.clip(cv, 0, 1) + 1e-4
    s_s = SMOOTH * PX
    slope_s = g(slope * wgt, s_s) / g(wgt, s_s)
    m = slope_s / HW                                            # u per s unit
    return m, mask, np.clip(cv, 0, 1), img


def save(name, m, mask, coh, out_h):
    enc = np.stack([np.clip(0.5 + m * SCALE, 0, 1), mask, np.clip(coh, 0, 1)], -1).astype(np.float32)
    enc = cv2.resize(enc, (OUT_W, out_h), interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)
    Image.fromarray(np.clip(enc * 255 + 0.5, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)).save(os.path.join(A, name))


def debug(tag, img, m, mask):
    if not dbg:
        return
    os.makedirs(dbg, exist_ok=True)
    v = np.clip(img, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8).copy()
    H, W = v.shape[:2]
    for y in range(6, H - 6, 14):
        for x in range(6, W - 6, 14):
            sl = m[y, x] * HW
            n = (1 + sl * sl) ** 0.5
            dx, dy = 6 * sl / n, 6 / n
            col = (255, 255, 0) if mask[y, x] > 0.5 else (90, 90, 90)
            cv2.line(v, (int(x - dx), int(y - dy)), (int(x + dx), int(y + dy)), col, 1, cv2.LINE_AA)
    Image.fromarray(v[::-1]).save(os.path.join(dbg, f"flow_{tag}.png"))            # far end on top, as on screen


rep = {}
N = np.asarray(Image.open(os.path.join(A, "proj05_N.png")).convert("RGBA")).astype(np.float32)
m, mask, coh, img = flow_of(N[..., :3], N[..., 3] / 255.0, lut["N"]["s1"] - lut["N"]["s0"], wrap=False)
save("proj05_WN.png", m, mask, coh, 240)
debug("N", img, m, mask)
rep["N"] = dict(mean_abs_slope_world=round(float(np.abs(m * HW)[(mask > 0.5) & (coh > 0.5)].mean()), 3), flow_area_of_covered=round(float((mask > 0.5)[coh > 0.5].mean()), 3))
T = np.asarray(Image.open(os.path.join(A, "proj05_T.png")).convert("RGB")).astype(np.float32)
m, mask, coh, img = flow_of(T, np.ones(T.shape[:2], np.float32), lut["T"]["L"], wrap=True)
save("proj05_WT.png", m, mask, coh, 84)
debug("T", img, m, mask)
rep["T"] = dict(mean_abs_slope_world=round(float(np.abs(m * HW)[mask > 0.5].mean()), 3), flow_area=round(float((mask > 0.5).mean()), 3))
meta = dict(scale=SCALE, half_width_u=HW, note="R = 0.5 + m * scale (m = du/ds along the approved streaks), G = flow mask, B = layer coverage", **rep)
with open(os.path.join(A, "proj05_flow.json"), "w") as f:
    json.dump(meta, f, indent=1)
print(json.dumps(meta))

entries.description:
Use this tool to create a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.
It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool

Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:

- Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
- Non-trivial and complex tasks - Tasks that require careful planning or multiple operations
- Plan mode - When using plan mode, create a task list to track the work
- User explicitly requests todo list - When the user directly asks you to use the todo list
- User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as tasks
- When you start working on a task - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
- After completing a task - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up tasks discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Skip using this tool when:
- There is only a single, straightforward task
- The task is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
- The task can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
- The task is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial task to do. In this case you are better off just doing the task directly.

## Task Fields

- **subject**: A brief, actionable title in imperative form (e.g., "Fix authentication bug in login flow")
- **description**: What needs to be done
- **activeForm** (optional): Present continuous form shown in the spinner when the task is in_progress (e.g., "Fixing authentication bug"). If omitted, the spinner shows the subject instead.

All tasks are created with status `pending`.

## Tips

- Create tasks with clear, specific subjects that describe the outcome
- After creating tasks, use TaskUpdate to set up dependencies (blocks/blockedBy) if needed
- Check TaskList first to avoid creating duplicate tasks

**Mark tasks as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a task
- When a task is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned tasks as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call TaskList to find your next task

- ONLY mark a task as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the task as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new task describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a task as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete tasks:**
- When a task is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the task

**Update task details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between tasks

## Fields You Can Update

- **status**: The task status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the task title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the task description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the task owner (agent name)
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the task (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark tasks that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark tasks that must complete before this one can start

## Status Workflow

Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`

Use `deleted` to permanently remove a task.

## Staleness

Make sure to read a task's latest state using `TaskGet` before updating it.

## Examples

Mark task as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```

Mark task as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```

Delete a task:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```

Claim a task by setting owner:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "owner": "my-name"}
```

Set up task dependencies:
```json
{"taskId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

"""Screen 05 `?proj05=1&projnear05=1` — HIGH-RESOLUTION NEAR TILE (plan in qa/pilot05/proj/flow2/NOTES.md, part 2).

Why: while riding, the near water switches from the exact layer E (sharp only from the locked camera) to the near layer N
and the tile T, both stored at 24 texels per world unit along the river, while the screen near Benny needs 100+ -> the
approved swirls turn into a pastel smear 8-17 u into the ride. The crisp approved detail that exists is the NEAREST
water of the locked view (E: 230-280 rows per unit at s 130, 53 at s 137.5). This tool resamples exactly that water out of
E (through its LUT, no new artwork, no invented texture) into a tile that the shader repeats along the river.

  proj05_T2.png   W x H RGB, u -1..1 across (columns), s in [A, A + L] along (rows, row 0 = s A); loaded with
                  MirroredRepeatWrapping along s (seamless, period 2 L) + mipmaps; outside each row's visible u-range the
                  row is reflected (ping-pong) about its visible edges.
  proj05_WT2.png  flow map of T2 (tools/proj05/flow_bake.py flow_of: R = 0.5 + du/ds * scale, G = flow mask, B = 1);
                  the shader flips the slope on mirrored periods.
  proj05_near.json  extents + resolution report.
usage: python3 -I tools/proj05/near_bake.py <assets/textures/water05> [--w=1024] [--h=768] [--a=130.5] [--l=7]
                  [--ss=3] (supersampling per axis) [--margin=0.015] (u kept away from the visible edge)"""
import json, os, sys
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
from scipy.ndimage import map_coordinates, minimum_filter1d, maximum_filter1d, gaussian_filter1d

pos = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if not a.startswith("--")]
opt = dict(a[2:].split("=", 1) for a in sys.argv[1:] if a.startswith("--") and "=" in a)
DIR = pos[0]
W, H = int(opt.get("w", 1024)), int(opt.get("h", 768))
A, L = float(opt.get("a", 130.5)), float(opt.get("l", 7.0))
SS = int(opt.get("ss", 3))
MARGIN = float(opt.get("margin", 0.015))

lut = json.load(open(os.path.join(DIR, "proj05_lut.json")))
Ej = lut["E"]
E = np.asarray(Image.open(os.path.join(DIR, "proj05_E.png")).convert("RGBA")).astype(np.float32) / 255.0
NE, WE = E.shape[:2]
sg = np.linspace(Ej["s0"], Ej["s1"], Ej["n"])
Vg, cg, wg = np.array(Ej["V"]), np.array(Ej["c"]), np.array(Ej["w"])

# visible (valid) u-range per E row, read from E's own alpha (not the LUT margin), smoothed along s
alpha = E[..., 3]
rows_lo = np.full(NE, np.nan); rows_hi = np.full(NE, np.nan)
for y in range(NE):
    xs = np.nonzero(alpha[y] > 0.9)[0]
    if len(xs) > 8:
        rows_lo[y], rows_hi[y] = xs[0], xs[-1]
# row y -> s (invert V), then column -> u
Vrow = (np.arange(NE) + 0.5) / NE
s_row = np.interp(Vrow, Vg, sg)
c_row, w_row = np.interp(s_row, sg, cg), np.interp(s_row, sg, wg)
col2u = lambda x, c, w: c + ((x + 0.5) / WE - 0.5) * 2 * w
ok = np.isfinite(rows_lo)
ulo = np.where(ok, col2u(np.nan_to_num(rows_lo), c_row, w_row), np.nan)
uhi = np.where(ok, col2u(np.nan_to_num(rows_hi), c_row, w_row), np.nan)
i = np.arange(NE)
ulo, uhi = np.interp(i, i[ok], ulo[ok]), np.interp(i, i[ok], uhi[ok])
ulo = gaussian_filter1d(maximum_filter1d(ulo, 9), 4) + MARGIN          # shrink: never sample a partly valid edge texel
uhi = gaussian_filter1d(minimum_filter1d(uhi, 9), 4) - MARGIN


def sample(u, s):
    """E colour (display values) at river coords (u, s); u is first folded into the row's visible range"""
    lo, hi = np.interp(s, s_row, ulo), np.interp(s, s_row, uhi)
    span = np.maximum(hi - lo, 1e-3)
    t = np.mod(u - lo, 2 * span)
    uf = lo + np.where(t < span, t, 2 * span - t)                          # ping-pong reflection about the edges
    v = np.interp(s, sg, Vg); c = np.interp(s, sg, cg); w = np.interp(s, sg, wg)
    x = (0.5 + (uf - c) / (2 * w)) * WE - 0.5
    y = v * NE - 0.5
    return np.stack([map_coordinates(E[..., k], [y, x], order=1, mode="nearest") for k in range(3)], -1), (u >= lo) & (u <= hi)


# supersampled bake (SS x SS per texel, box filter): the source is denser than the tile across u everywhere and along s
# for s < 134, so averaging avoids aliasing the fine glints
acc = np.zeros((H, W, 3), np.float64); real = np.zeros((H, W), np.float64)
for oy in range(SS):
    for ox in range(SS):
        uu = -1 + (np.arange(W) + (ox + 0.5) / SS) / W * 2
        ss_ = A + (np.arange(H) + (oy + 0.5) / SS) / H * L
        U, S = np.meshgrid(uu, ss_)
        col, inside = sample(U.ravel(), S.ravel())
        acc += col.reshape(H, W, 3); real += inside.reshape(H, W)
T2 = acc / (SS * SS)
real /= SS * SS
Image.fromarray(np.clip(T2 * 255 + 0.5, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)).save(os.path.join(DIR, "proj05_T2.png"), optimize=True)

# flow map of the new tile with the existing flow_bake.flow_of (same structure-tensor method, same encoding)
src = open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "flow_bake.py")).read()
ns = {"__name__": "flow_bake_lib"}
argv0 = sys.argv
sys.argv = ["flow_bake.py", DIR]
exec(compile(src.split("\nrep = {}")[0], "flow_bake.py", "exec"), ns)
sys.argv = argv0
m, mask, coh, _ = ns["flow_of"]((T2 * 255).astype(np.float32), np.ones((H, W), np.float32), L, wrap=False)
out_h = int(round(L * 8))
ns["save"]("proj05_WT2.png", m, mask, coh, out_h)

# resolution report: texels per world unit (s is in world units, u = 1 is the river half width)
hw = ns["HW"]
dens_src = np.gradient(np.interp(sg, sg, Vg), sg) * NE
rep = dict(
    note="proj05 near tile (tools/proj05/near_bake.py); shader: ?proj05=1&projnear05=1 (src/vfx/waterRibbon.ts)",
    T2=dict(a=A, L=L, width=W, height=H, wrapT="mirrored", period=2 * L),
    texels_per_world_unit=dict(along=round(H / L, 1), across=round(W / (2 * hw), 1), old_N_T_along=24.0,
                              old_T_across=round(512 / (2 * hw), 1)),
    source_rows_per_world_unit={f"{s:.1f}": round(float(np.interp(s, sg, dens_src)), 1) for s in (130.5, 132, 134, 136, 137.5)},
    visible_u_range={f"{s:.1f}": [round(float(np.interp(s, s_row, ulo)), 3), round(float(np.interp(s, s_row, uhi)), 3)]
                     for s in (130.5, 132, 134, 136, 137.5)},
    share_of_texels_from_visible_water=round(float(real.mean()), 3),
    flow=dict(file="proj05_WT2.png", height=out_h, mean_abs_slope_world=round(float(np.abs(m * hw)[mask > 0.5].mean()), 3),
              flow_area=round(float((mask > 0.5).mean()), 3)),
)
json.dump(rep, open(os.path.join(DIR, "proj05_near.json"), "w"), indent=1)
print(json.dumps(rep, indent=1))

@@ -0,0 +1,111 @@
+"""Screen 05 `?proj05=1&projnear05=1` — HIGH-RESOLUTION NEAR TILE (plan in qa/pilot05/proj/flow2/NOTES.md, part 2).
+
+Why: while riding, the near water switches from the exact layer E (sharp only from the locked camera) to the near layer N
+and the tile T, both stored at 24 texels per world unit along the river, while the screen near Benny needs 100+ -> the
+approved swirls turn into a pastel smear 8-17 u into the ride. The crisp approved detail that exists is the NEAREST
+water of the locked view (E: 230-280 rows per unit at s 130, 53 at s 137.5). This tool resamples exactly that water out of
+E (through its LUT, no new artwork, no invented texture) into a tile that the shader repeats along the river.
+
+  proj05_T2.png   W x H RGB, u -1..1 across (columns), s in [A, A + L] along (rows, row 0 = s A); loaded with
+                  MirroredRepeatWrapping along s (seamless, period 2 L) + mipmaps; outside each row's visible u-range the
+                  row is reflected (ping-pong) about its visible edges.
+  proj05_WT2.png  flow map of T2 (tools/proj05/flow_bake.py flow_of: R = 0.5 + du/ds * scale, G = flow mask, B = 1);
+                  the shader flips the slope on mirrored periods.
+  proj05_near.json  extents + resolution report.
+usage: python3 -I tools/proj05/near_bake.py <assets/textures/water05> [--w=1024] [--h=768] [--a=130.5] [--l=7]
+                  [--ss=3] (supersampling per axis) [--margin=0.015] (u kept away from the visible edge)"""
+import json, os, sys
+import numpy as np
+from PIL import Image
+from scipy.ndimage import map_coordinates, minimum_filter1d, maximum_filter1d, gaussian_filter1d
+
+pos = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if not a.startswith("--")]
+opt = dict(a[2:].split("=", 1) for a in sys.argv[1:] if a.startswith("--") and "=" in a)
+DIR = pos[0]
+W, H = int(opt.get("w", 1024)), int(opt.get("h", 768))
+A, L = float(opt.get("a", 130.5)), float(opt.get("l", 7.0))
+SS = int(opt.get("ss", 3))
+MARGIN = float(opt.get("margin", 0.015))
+
+lut = json.load(open(os.path.join(DIR, "proj05_lut.json")))
+Ej = lut["E"]
+E = np.asarray(Image.open(os.path.join(DIR, "proj05_E.png")).convert("RGBA")).astype(np.float32) / 255.0
+NE, WE = E.shape[:2]
+sg = np.linspace(Ej["s0"], Ej["s1"], Ej["n"])
+Vg, cg, wg = np.array(Ej["V"]), np.array(Ej["c"]), np.array(Ej["w"])
+
+# visible (valid) u-range per E row, read from E's own alpha (not the LUT margin), smoothed along s
+alpha = E[..., 3]
+rows_lo = np.full(NE, np.nan); rows_hi = np.full(NE, np.nan)
+for y in range(NE):
+    xs = np.nonzero(alpha[y] > 0.9)[0]
+    if len(xs) > 8:
+        rows_lo[y], rows_hi[y] = xs[0], xs[-1]
+# row y -> s (invert V), then column -> u
+Vrow = (np.arange(NE) + 0.5) / NE
+s_row = np.interp(Vrow, Vg, sg)
+c_row, w_row = np.interp(s_row, sg, cg), np.interp(s_row, sg, wg)
+col2u = lambda x, c, w: c + ((x + 0.5) / WE - 0.5) * 2 * w
+ok = np.isfinite(rows_lo)
+ulo = np.where(ok, col2u(np.nan_to_num(rows_lo), c_row, w_row), np.nan)
+uhi = np.where(ok, col2u(np.nan_to_num(rows_hi), c_row, w_row), np.nan)
+i = np.arange(NE)
+ulo, uhi = np.interp(i, i[ok], ulo[ok]), np.interp(i, i[ok], uhi[ok])
+ulo = gaussian_filter1d(maximum_filter1d(ulo, 9), 4) + MARGIN          # shrink: never sample a partly valid edge texel
+uhi = gaussian_filter1d(minimum_filter1d(uhi, 9), 4) - MARGIN
+
+
+def sample(u, s):
+    """E colour (display values) at river coords (u, s); u is first folded into the row's visible range"""
+    lo, hi = np.interp(s, s_row, ulo), np.interp(s, s_row, uhi)
+    span = np.maximum(hi - lo, 1e-3)
+    t = np.mod(u - lo, 2 * span)
+    uf = lo + np.where(t < span, t, 2 * span - t)                          # ping-pong reflection about the edges
+    v = np.interp(s, sg, Vg); c = np.interp(s, sg, cg); w = np.interp(s, sg, wg)
+    x = (0.5 + (uf - c) / (2 * w)) * WE - 0.5
+    y = v * NE - 0.5
+    return np.stack([map_coordinates(E[..., k], [y, x], order=1, mode="nearest") for k in range(3)], -1), (u >= lo) & (u <= hi)
+
+
+# supersampled bake (SS x SS per texel, box filter): the source is denser than the tile across u everywhere and along s
+# for s < 134, so averaging avoids aliasing the fine glints
+acc = np.zeros((H, W, 3), np.float64); real = np.zeros((H, W), np.float64)
+for oy in range(SS):
+    for ox in range(SS):
+        uu = -1 + (np.arange(W) + (ox + 0.5) / SS) / W * 2
+        ss_ = A + (np.arange(H) + (oy + 0.5) / SS) / H * L
+        U, S = np.meshgrid(uu, ss_)
+        col, inside = sample(U.ravel(), S.ravel())
+        acc += col.reshape(H, W, 3); real += inside.reshape(H, W)
+T2 = acc / (SS * SS)
+real /= SS * SS
+Image.fromarray(np.clip(T2 * 255 + 0.5, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)).save(os.path.join(DIR, "proj05_T2.png"), optimize=True)
+
+# flow map of the new tile with the existing flow_bake.flow_of (same structure-tensor method, same encoding)
+src = open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "flow_bake.py")).read()
+ns = {"__name__": "flow_bake_lib"}
+argv0 = sys.argv
+sys.argv = ["flow_bake.py", DIR]
+exec(compile(src.split("\nrep = {}")[0], "flow_bake.py", "exec"), ns)
+sys.argv = argv0
+m, mask, coh, _ = ns["flow_of"]((T2 * 255).astype(np.float32), np.ones((H, W), np.float32), L, wrap=False)
+out_h = int(round(L * 8))
+ns["save"]("proj05_WT2.png", m, mask, coh, out_h)
+
+# resolution report: texels per world unit (s is in world units, u = 1 is the river half width)
+hw = ns["HW"]
+dens_src = np.gradient(np.interp(sg, sg, Vg), sg) * NE
+rep = dict(
+    note="proj05 near tile (tools/proj05/near_bake.py); shader: ?proj05=1&projnear05=1 (src/vfx/waterRibbon.ts)",
+    T2=dict(a=A, L=L, width=W, height=H, wrapT="mirrored", period=2 * L),
+    texels_per_world_unit=dict(along=round(H / L, 1), across=round(W / (2 * hw), 1), old_N_T_along=24.0,
+                              old_T_across=round(512 / (2 * hw), 1)),
+    source_rows_per_world_unit={f"{s:.1f}": round(float(np.interp(s, sg, dens_src)), 1) for s in (130.5, 132, 134, 136, 137.5)},
+    visible_u_range={f"{s:.1f}": [round(float(np.interp(s, s_row, ulo)), 3), round(float(np.interp(s, s_row, uhi)), 3)]
+                     for s in (130.5, 132, 134, 136, 137.5)},
+    share_of_texels_from_visible_water=round(float(real.mean()), 3),
+    flow=dict(file="proj05_WT2.png", height=out_h, mean_abs_slope_world=round(float(np.abs(m * hw)[mask > 0.5].mean()), 3),
+              flow_area=round(float((mask > 0.5).mean()), 3)),
+)
+json.dump(rep, open(os.path.join(DIR, "proj05_near.json"), "w"), indent=1)
+print(json.dumps(rep, indent=1))

"""Screen 05 `?proj05=1&projnear05=1` — HIGH-RESOLUTION NEAR TILE (plan in qa/pilot05/proj/flow2/NOTES.md, part 2).

Why: while riding, the near water switches from the exact layer E (sharp only from the locked camera) to the near layer N
and the tile T, both stored at 24 texels per world unit along the river, while the screen near Benny needs 100+ -> the
approved swirls turn into a pastel smear 8-17 u into the ride. The crisp approved detail that exists is the NEAREST
water of the locked view (E: 230-280 rows per unit at s 130, 53 at s 137.5). This tool resamples exactly that water out of
E (through its LUT, no new artwork, no invented texture) into a tile that the shader repeats along the river.

  proj05_T2.png   W x H RGB, u -1..1 across (columns), s in [A, A + L] along (rows, row 0 = s A); loaded with
                  MirroredRepeatWrapping along s (seamless, period 2 L) + mipmaps; outside each row's visible u-range the
                  row is reflected (ping-pong) about its visible edges.
  proj05_WT2.png  flow map of T2 (tools/proj05/flow_bake.py flow_of: R = 0.5 + du/ds * scale, G = flow mask, B = 1);
                  the shader flips the slope on mirrored periods.
  proj05_near.json  extents + resolution report.
usage: python3 -I tools/proj05/near_bake.py <assets/textures/water05> [--w=1024] [--h=768] [--a=130.5] [--l=7]
                  [--ss=3] (supersampling per axis) [--margin=0.015] (u kept away from the visible edge)"""
import json, os, sys
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
from scipy.ndimage import map_coordinates, minimum_filter1d, maximum_filter1d, gaussian_filter1d

pos = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if not a.startswith("--")]
opt = dict(a[2:].split("=", 1) for a in sys.argv[1:] if a.startswith("--") and "=" in a)
DIR = pos[0]
W, H = int(opt.get("w", 1024)), int(opt.get("h", 768))
A, L = float(opt.get("a", 130.5)), float(opt.get("l", 7.0))
SS = int(opt.get("ss", 3))
MARGIN = float(opt.get("margin", 0.015))

lut = json.load(open(os.path.join(DIR, "proj05_lut.json")))
Ej = lut["E"]
E = np.asarray(Image.open(os.path.join(DIR, "proj05_E.png")).convert("RGBA")).astype(np.float32) / 255.0
NE, WE = E.shape[:2]
sg = np.linspace(Ej["s0"], Ej["s1"], Ej["n"])
Vg, cg, wg = np.array(Ej["V"]), np.array(Ej["c"]), np.array(Ej["w"])

# visible (valid) u-range per E row, read from E's own alpha (not the LUT margin), smoothed along s
alpha = E[..., 3]
rows_lo = np.full(NE, np.nan); rows_hi = np.full(NE, np.nan)
for y in range(NE):
    xs = np.nonzero(alpha[y] > 0.9)[0]
    if len(xs) > 8:
        rows_lo[y], rows_hi[y] = xs[0], xs[-1]

"""Screen 05 `?proj05=1&projnear05=1` — HIGH-RESOLUTION NEAR TILE (plan in qa/pilot05/proj/flow2/NOTES.md, part 2).

Why: while riding, the near water switches from the exact layer E (sharp only from the locked camera) to the near layer N
and the tile T, both stored at 24 texels per world unit along the river, while the screen near Benny needs 100+ -> the
approved swirls turn into a pastel smear 8-17 u into the ride. The crisp approved detail that exists is the NEAREST
water of the locked view (E: 230-280 rows per unit at s 130, 53 at s 137.5). This tool resamples exactly that water out of
E (through its LUT, no new artwork, no invented texture) into a tile that the shader repeats along the river.

  proj05_T2.png   W x H RGB, u -1..1 across (columns), s in [A, A + L] along (rows, row 0 = s A); loaded with
                  MirroredRepeatWrapping along s (seamless, period 2 L) + mipmaps; outside each row's visible u-range the
                  row is reflected (ping-pong) about its visible edges.
  proj05_WT2.png  flow map of T2 (tools/proj05/flow_bake.py flow_of: R = 0.5 + du/ds * scale, G = flow mask, B = 1);
                  the shader flips the slope on mirrored periods.
  proj05_near.json  extents + resolution report.
usage: python3 -I tools/proj05/near_bake.py <assets/textures/water05> [--w=1024] [--h=768] [--a=130.5] [--l=7]

import json, os, sys
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
from scipy.ndimage import map_coordinates, minimum_filter1d, maximum_filter1d, gaussian_filter1d

pos = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if not a.startswith("--")]
opt = dict(a[2:].split("=", 1) for a in sys.argv[1:] if a.startswith("--") and "=" in a)
DIR = pos[0]
W, H = int(opt.get("w", 1024)), int(opt.get("h", 768))
A, L = float(opt.get("a", 130.5)), float(opt.get("l", 7.0))
SS = int(opt.get("ss", 3))
MARGIN = float(opt.get("margin", 0.015))

lut = json.load(open(os.path.join(DIR, "proj05_lut.json")))
Ej = lut["E"]
E = np.asarray(Image.open(os.path.join(DIR, "proj05_E.png")).convert("RGBA")).astype(np.float32) / 255.0
NE, WE = E.shape[:2]
sg = np.linspace(Ej["s0"], Ej["s1"], Ej["n"])
Vg, cg, wg = np.array(Ej["V"]), np.array(Ej["c"]), np.array(Ej["w"])

# visible (valid) u-range per E row, read from E's own alpha (not the LUT margin), smoothed along s
alpha = E[..., 3]
rows_lo = np.full(NE, np.nan); rows_hi = np.full(NE, np.nan)
for y in range(NE):
    xs = np.nonzero(alpha[y] > 0.9)[0]
    if len(xs) > 8:

Vrow = (np.arange(NE) + 0.5) / NE
s_row = np.interp(Vrow, Vg, sg)
c_row, w_row = np.interp(s_row, sg, cg), np.interp(s_row, sg, wg)
col2u = lambda x, c, w: c + ((x + 0.5) / WE - 0.5) * 2 * w
ok = np.isfinite(rows_lo)
ulo = np.where(ok, col2u(np.nan_to_num(rows_lo), c_row, w_row), np.nan)
uhi = np.where(ok, col2u(np.nan_to_num(rows_hi), c_row, w_row), np.nan)
i = np.arange(NE)
ulo, uhi = np.interp(i, i[ok], ulo[ok]), np.interp(i, i[ok], uhi[ok])
ulo = gaussian_filter1d(maximum_filter1d(ulo, 9), 4) + MARGIN          # shrink: never sample a partly valid edge texel
uhi = gaussian_filter1d(minimum_filter1d(uhi, 9), 4) - MARGIN


# FILL (2026-11-16, after the first bake showed a kaleidoscope): near the start of the tile only the river centre is
# visible in the locked view (u ±0.28 at s 130.5), so instead of bouncing that strip across the river, each column u
# reads REAL visible approved water from the first s where that column becomes visible: per-column shift along s,
# smooth in u (no mirror symmetry; the crisp centre keeps shift 0). The sides then come from E at 30-75 rows / unit —
# what the riding view needs there (scripts/proj05-ride-probe.mjs: 25-50 px / unit 2-6 u ahead of Benny).

lo_scan, hi_scan = np.interp(s_scan, s_row, ulo), np.interp(s_scan, s_row, uhi)
uc = np.clip(uu_g, -0.985, 0.985)
vis = (uc[:, None] >= lo_scan[None]) & (uc[:, None] <= hi_scan[None])
first = np.where(vis.any(1), s_scan[np.argmax(vis, 1)], s_scan[-1])
need = np.maximum(first + SHIFT_PAD - A, 0.0)
need = np.where(np.abs(uu_g) < 0.15, 0.0, need)                 # Benny's lane: always the crisp nearest water
# monotone away from the centre, then smoothed (and never below what is needed)
mid = len(uu_g) // 2
need[mid:] = np.maximum.accumulate(need[mid:]); need[:mid + 1] = np.maximum.accumulate(need[:mid + 1][::-1])[::-1]
shift_g = gaussian_filter1d(need, 6)
shift_g = np.maximum(shift_g, need)
shift_g = gaussian_filter1d(shift_g, 3)


def shift_of(u):
    return np.interp(u, uu_g, shift_g)


def sample(u, s):
    """E colour (display values) at river coords (u, s): the column's s is first moved to where u is visible; anything
    still outside the row's visible range is folded back into it (rare, only at the river's very edge)"""
    s = s + shift_of(u)
    u = np.clip(u, -0.985, 0.985)
    lo, hi = np.interp(s, s_row, ulo), np.interp(s, s_row, uhi)

# for s < 134, so averaging avoids aliasing the fine glints
acc = np.zeros((H, W, 3), np.float64); real = np.zeros((H, W), np.float64)
for oy in range(SS):
    for ox in range(SS):
        uu = -1 + (np.arange(W) + (ox + 0.5) / SS) / W * 2

        U, S = np.meshgrid(uu, ss_)
        col, inside = sample(U.ravel(), S.ravel())
        acc += col.reshape(H, W, 3); real += inside.reshape(H, W)

Image.fromarray(np.clip(T2 * 255 + 0.5, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)).save(os.path.join(DIR, "proj05_T2.png"), optimize=True)

# flow map of the new tile with the existing flow_bake.flow_of (same structure-tensor method, same encoding)
src = open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "flow_bake.py")).read()
ns = {"__name__": "flow_bake_lib"}
argv0 = sys.argv
sys.argv = ["flow_bake.py", DIR]
exec(compile(src.split("\nrep = {}")[0], "flow_bake.py", "exec"), ns)
sys.argv = argv0
m, mask, coh, _ = ns["flow_of"]((T2 * 255).astype(np.float32), np.ones((H, W), np.float32), L, wrap=False)
out_h = int(round(L * 8))
ns["save"]("proj05_WT2.png", m, mask, coh, out_h)

# resolution report: texels per world unit (s is in world units, u = 1 is the river half width)
hw = ns["HW"]
dens_src = np.gradient(np.interp(sg, sg, Vg), sg) * NE
rep = dict(
    note="proj05 near tile (tools/proj05/near_bake.py); shader: ?proj05=1&projnear05=1 (src/vfx/waterRibbon.ts)",
    T2=dict(a=A, L=L, width=W, height=H, wrapT="mirrored", period=2 * L),
    texels_per_world_unit=dict(along=round(H / L, 1), across=round(W / (2 * hw), 1), old_N_T_along=24.0,

    source_rows_per_world_unit={f"{s:.1f}": round(float(np.interp(s, sg, dens_src)), 1) for s in (130.5, 132, 134, 136, 137.5)},
    visible_u_range={f"{s:.1f}": [round(float(np.interp(s, s_row, ulo)), 3), round(float(np.interp(s, s_row, uhi)), 3)]

    share_of_texels_from_visible_water=round(float(real.mean()), 3),
    column_shift_s={f"{u:+.1f}": round(float(shift_of(u)), 2) for u in (-0.9, -0.7, -0.5, -0.3, 0.0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9)},
    flow=dict(file="proj05_WT2.png", height=out_h, mean_abs_slope_world=round(float(np.abs(m * hw)[mask > 0.5].mean()), 3),

)
json.dump(rep, open(os.path.join(DIR, "proj05_near.json"), "w"), indent=1)
print(json.dumps(rep, indent=1))

"""Screen 05 `?proj05=1&projnear05=1` — HIGH-RESOLUTION NEAR TILE (plan in qa/pilot05/proj/flow2/NOTES.md, part 2).

Why: while riding, the near water switches from the exact layer E (sharp only from the locked camera) to the near layer N
and the tile T, both stored at 24 texels per world unit along the river, while the screen near Benny needs 100+ -> the
approved swirls turn into a pastel smear 8-17 u into the ride. The crisp approved detail that exists is the NEAREST
water of the locked view (E: 230-280 rows per unit at s 130, 53 at s 137.5). This tool resamples exactly that water out of
E (through its LUT, no new artwork, no invented texture) into a tile that the shader repeats along the river.

  proj05_T2.png   W x H RGB, u -1..1 across (columns), s in [A, A + L] along (rows, row 0 = s A); loaded with
                  MirroredRepeatWrapping along s (seamless, period 2 L) + mipmaps; outside each row's visible u-range the
                  row is reflected (ping-pong) about its visible edges.
  proj05_WT2.png  flow map of T2 (tools/proj05/flow_bake.py flow_of: R = 0.5 + du/ds * scale, G = flow mask, B = 1);
                  the shader flips the slope on mirrored periods.
  proj05_near.json  extents + resolution report.
usage: python3 -I tools/proj05/near_bake.py <assets/textures/water05> [--w=1024] [--h=768] [--a=130.5] [--l=7]
                  [--ss=3] (supersampling per axis) [--margin=0.015] (u kept away from the visible edge)"""
import json, os, sys
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
from scipy.ndimage import map_coordinates, minimum_filter1d, maximum_filter1d, gaussian_filter1d

pos = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if not a.startswith("--")]
opt = dict(a[2:].split("=", 1) for a in sys.argv[1:] if a.startswith("--") and "=" in a)
DIR = pos[0]
W, H = int(opt.get("w", 1024)), int(opt.get("h", 768))
A, L = float(opt.get("a", 130.5)), float(opt.get("l", 7.0))
SS = int(opt.get("ss", 3))
MARGIN = float(opt.get("margin", 0.015))

lut = json.load(open(os.path.join(DIR, "proj05_lut.json")))
Ej = lut["E"]
E = np.asarray(Image.open(os.path.join(DIR, "proj05_E.png")).convert("RGBA")).astype(np.float32) / 255.0
NE, WE = E.shape[:2]
sg = np.linspace(Ej["s0"], Ej["s1"], Ej["n"])
Vg, cg, wg = np.array(Ej["V"]), np.array(Ej["c"]), np.array(Ej["w"])

# visible (valid) u-range per E row, read from E's own alpha (not the LUT margin), smoothed along s
alpha = E[..., 3]
rows_lo = np.full(NE, np.nan); rows_hi = np.full(NE, np.nan)
for y in range(NE):
    xs = np.nonzero(alpha[y] > 0.9)[0]
    if len(xs) > 8:
        rows_lo[y], rows_hi[y] = xs[0], xs[-1]
# row y -> s (invert V), then column -> u
Vrow = (np.arange(NE) + 0.5) / NE
s_row = np.interp(Vrow, Vg, sg)
c_row, w_row = np.interp(s_row, sg, cg), np.interp(s_row, sg, wg)
col2u = lambda x, c, w: c + ((x + 0.5) / WE - 0.5) * 2 * w
ok = np.isfinite(rows_lo)
ulo = np.where(ok, col2u(np.nan_to_num(rows_lo), c_row, w_row), np.nan)
uhi = np.where(ok, col2u(np.nan_to_num(rows_hi), c_row, w_row), np.nan)
i = np.arange(NE)
ulo, uhi = np.interp(i, i[ok], ulo[ok]), np.interp(i, i[ok], uhi[ok])
ulo = gaussian_filter1d(maximum_filter1d(ulo, 9), 4) + MARGIN          # shrink: never sample a partly valid edge texel
uhi = gaussian_filter1d(minimum_filter1d(uhi, 9), 4) - MARGIN


# FILL (2026-11-16, after the first bake showed a kaleidoscope): near the start of the tile only the river centre is
# visible in the locked view (u ±0.28 at s 130.5), so instead of bouncing that strip across the river, each column u
# reads REAL visible approved water from the first s where that column becomes visible: per-column shift along s,
# smooth in u (no mirror symmetry; the crisp centre keeps shift 0). The sides then come from E at 30-75 rows / unit —
# what the riding view needs there (scripts/proj05-ride-probe.mjs: 25-50 px / unit 2-6 u ahead of Benny).
SHIFT_PAD = float(opt.get("pad", 0.4))         # extra s beyond the first visible row (stay off the visible edge)
uu_g = np.linspace(-1, 1, 401)
s_scan = np.linspace(A, Ej["s1"] - L - 0.5, 1200)
lo_scan, hi_scan = np.interp(s_scan, s_row, ulo), np.interp(s_scan, s_row, uhi)
uc = np.clip(uu_g, -0.985, 0.985)
vis = (uc[:, None] >= lo_scan[None]) & (uc[:, None] <= hi_scan[None])
first = np.where(vis.any(1), s_scan[np.argmax(vis, 1)], s_scan[-1])
need = np.maximum(first + SHIFT_PAD - A, 0.0)
need = np.where(np.abs(uu_g) < 0.15, 0.0, need)                 # Benny's lane: always the crisp nearest water
# monotone away from the centre, then smoothed (and never below what is needed)
mid = len(uu_g) // 2
need[mid:] = np.maximum.accumulate(need[mid:]); need[:mid + 1] = np.maximum.accumulate(need[:mid + 1][::-1])[::-1]
shift_g = gaussian_filter1d(need, 6)
shift_g = np.maximum(shift_g, need)
shift_g = gaussian_filter1d(shift_g, 3)


def shift_of(u):
    return np.interp(u, uu_g, shift_g)


def sample(u, s):
    """E colour (display values) at river coords (u, s): the column's s is first moved to where u is visible; anything
    still outside the row's visible range is folded back into it (rare, only at the river's very edge)"""
    s = s + shift_of(u)
    u = np.clip(u, -0.985, 0.985)
    lo, hi = np.interp(s, s_row, ulo), np.interp(s, s_row, uhi)
    span = np.maximum(hi - lo, 1e-3)
    t = np.mod(u - lo, 2 * span)
    uf = lo + np.where(t < span, t, 2 * span - t)                          # ping-pong reflection about the edges
    v = np.interp(s, sg, Vg); c = np.interp(s, sg, cg); w = np.interp(s, sg, wg)
    x = (0.5 + (uf - c) / (2 * w)) * WE - 0.5
    y = v * NE - 0.5
    # alpha-weighted (premultiplied) so E texels without data (rgb 0) never bleed in as black lines
    a = map_coordinates(E[..., 3], [y, x], order=1, mode="nearest")
    rgb = np.stack([map_coordinates(E[..., k] * E[..., 3], [y, x], order=1, mode="nearest") for k in range(3)], -1)
    return rgb / np.maximum(a, 1e-4)[:, None], (u >= lo) & (u <= hi), a


# supersampled bake (SS x SS per texel, box filter): the source is denser than the tile across u everywhere and along s
# for s < 134, so averaging avoids aliasing the fine glints
acc = np.zeros((H, W, 3), np.float64); real = np.zeros((H, W), np.float64)
for oy in range(SS):
    for ox in range(SS):
        uu = -1 + (np.arange(W) + (ox + 0.5) / SS) / W * 2
        ss_ = A + (np.arange(H) + (oy + 0.5) / SS) / H * L
        U, S = np.meshgrid(uu, ss_)
        col, inside = sample(U.ravel(), S.ravel())
        acc += col.reshape(H, W, 3); real += inside.reshape(H, W)
T2 = acc / (SS * SS)
real /= SS * SS
Image.fromarray(np.clip(T2 * 255 + 0.5, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)).save(os.path.join(DIR, "proj05_T2.png"), optimize=True)

# flow map of the new tile with the existing flow_bake.flow_of (same structure-tensor method, same encoding)
src = open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "flow_bake.py")).read()
ns = {"__name__": "flow_bake_lib"}
argv0 = sys.argv
sys.argv = ["flow_bake.py", DIR]
exec(compile(src.split("\nrep = {}")[0], "flow_bake.py", "exec"), ns)
sys.argv = argv0
m, mask, coh, _ = ns["flow_of"]((T2 * 255).astype(np.float32), np.ones((H, W), np.float32), L, wrap=False)
out_h = int(round(L * 8))
ns["save"]("proj05_WT2.png", m, mask, coh, out_h)

# resolution report: texels per world unit (s is in world units, u = 1 is the river half width)
hw = ns["HW"]
dens_src = np.gradient(np.interp(sg, sg, Vg), sg) * NE
rep = dict(
    note="proj05 near tile (tools/proj05/near_bake.py); shader: ?proj05=1&projnear05=1 (src/vfx/waterRibbon.ts)",
    T2=dict(a=A, L=L, width=W, height=H, wrapT="mirrored", period=2 * L),
    texels_per_world_unit=dict(along=round(H / L, 1), across=round(W / (2 * hw), 1), old_N_T_along=24.0,
                              old_T_across=round(512 / (2 * hw), 1)),
    source_rows_per_world_unit={f"{s:.1f}": round(float(np.interp(s, sg, dens_src)), 1) for s in (130.5, 132, 134, 136, 137.5)},
    visible_u_range={f"{s:.1f}": [round(float(np.interp(s, s_row, ulo)), 3), round(float(np.interp(s, s_row, uhi)), 3)]
                     for s in (130.5, 132, 134, 136, 137.5)},
    share_of_texels_from_visible_water=round(float(real.mean()), 3),
    column_shift_s={f"{u:+.1f}": round(float(shift_of(u)), 2) for u in (-0.9, -0.7, -0.5, -0.3, 0.0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9)},
    flow=dict(file="proj05_WT2.png", height=out_h, mean_abs_slope_world=round(float(np.abs(m * hw)[mask > 0.5].mean()), 3),
              flow_area=round(float((mask > 0.5).mean()), 3)),
)
json.dump(rep, open(os.path.join(DIR, "proj05_near.json"), "w"), indent=1)
print(json.dumps(rep, indent=1))
